title: UK National Accounts, The Blue Book 2026 (ONS, 09:30 London) — the compendium, two days after the Autumn Budget and two days after the FOMC
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/uknationalaccountsthebluebook2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200) by this event's own lane — reads verbatim 'UK National Accounts, The Blue Book: 2026', 'Provisional release date: 30 October 2026 9:30am', 'This release is not yet published', summary 'National accounts statistics including national and sector accounts, industrial analyses and environmental accounts', with the accredited-official-statistics kitemark. The page's own dataLayer carries release-status 'upcoming', release-date '2026/10/30', release-time '09:30'. Cadence scraped FIRST-PARTY this session rather than search-relayed, from the ONS's own twelve compendium landing pages (HTTP 200 each): 2014-10-31, 2015-10-30, 2016-07-29, 2017-10-31, 2018-07-31, 2019-10-31, 2020-10-30, 2021-10-29, 2022-10-31, 2023-10-31, 2024-10-31, 2025-10-31 — all twelve on the LAST WORKING DAY of their publication month, with no exception, and the last seven consecutive editions all in October. 2026-10-31 is a Saturday, so the last working day of October 2026 is Friday 2026-10-30, exactly the provisional date. Filed estimate on three counts: the ONS itself labels the date PROVISIONAL (its sibling releases dated the same month, e.g. gdpmonthlyestimateukaugust2026, carry a plain 'Release date:' instead — the distinction is the publisher's, not this lane's), market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a foreign national statistics institute, and this lane does not self-confirm
notes: Canonical file written 2026-09-10 by the never-assessed initial research of this id, which existed only as proposals/uk-blue-book-2026-10-30.from-uk-quarterly-national-accounts-2026-09-30.json (read in full first; it stays where it is and is now shadowed). The proposing lane explicitly disclaimed any impact measurement — 'the LOW tier is inherited from the ONS family rather than argued from its own tape'. This lane MEASURED it and the tier survives. Central content finding, and it is the PUBLISHER'S OWN WORDS rather than an inference: the Blue Book compendium introduces no new aggregates. Its Release policy section states 'Data are consistent with ... our GDP quarterly national accounts bulletin, published on 30 September' in four consecutive editions fetched direct this session (BB2022, BB2023, BB2024, BB2025 background notes, HTTP 200 each). For 2026 that makes the compendium the THIRD publication of the same numbers: impact articles 2026-08-20 (revisions public in full), QNA 2026-09-30 (incorporated into official estimates), compendium 2026-10-30 (consistent with the QNA) — 71 and 30 days stale respectively on publication day. Even its freshest inputs are public first: UK monthly GDP, Index of Production and Index of Services for August 2026 all publish 2026-10-15 07:00 (ONS, fetched direct, a firm 'Release date' not a provisional one). MEASURED TAPE, first-party, across all twelve Blue Book publication days 2014-2025 against every other session since 2014-01-01: IGLT.L 1.17x an ordinary day (t = 0.82, n = 12), ^FTSE 0.74x (t = -1.35), ^TNX 0.88x (t = -0.42), SPY 0.88x (t = -0.53), ^VIX 0.91x (t = -0.46), GBPUSD=X 0.80x (t = -1.49, n = 10). Not one ratio is significantly above 1.0. The only ratio above 1.0 at all is the gilt one, and it is ENTIRELY the two Budget-adjacent editions: 2024-10-31 (-0.880%, the day after the 2024-10-30 Budget) and 2021-10-29 (-0.482%, two days after the 2021-10-27 Budget) are the largest and fifth-largest moves in the set; drop those two and the other ten run 1.05x at t = 0.21, a clean null. 2026-10-30 IS THE THIRD SUCH EDITION — Budget D+2, the same offset as 2021 — which makes this entry's operational job an attribution refusal, not a signal: 41 tracked events sit within five days, including fomc-2026-10-28 (high, confirmed) and uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28 on the same day as each other, pce-2026-10-29 and gdp-q3-2026-advance-2026-10-29 (both high, confirmed), and eci-q3-2026-10-30 (high, confirmed) plus boj-decision-2026-10-30 on the day itself. Autumn-Budget D+2 is measurably QUIETER than an ordinary day on every series tested (IGLT.L 0.54x t = -1.86, ^FTSE 0.54x, SPY 0.40x t = -4.34, n = 4).
